schema_conformance.note: contracts/participant-observation.schema.json sets additionalProperties false and admits none of observer_id, contributed_to_build, verdict, candidate_commit, candidate_tree or base_commit. No schema in contracts/ admits both, and nothing grades reports/observations/ against a schema, so this file is gate-readable and not schema-valid. Recorded rather than smoothed.

design_judgement.question: coherent design, or an accumulation that passes its own tests
design_judgement.reading: Coherent in its centre and accumulated at its edge. The centre is genuinely well-made: one mask rather than eight private scanners, provenance followed to bindings rather than name lists matched, a fixpoint rather than a pattern, fail-closed classification, and a corpus that names the refusal each case must produce rather than counting them. Those are the right shapes and they survived every attack this reading generated except one. The edge is accumulated: the frame path is a special case that skips four rules, and it is the path the primary claim depends on. Ten of the eleven survivors and near-misses found here sit in that one branch. The structural work readings six through nine split over - making the frame the only way to build a witness prompt - is not what this reading finds owed. What is owed is narrower and needs no cross-file imports: the frame path currently returns early, and everything that returns early is ungraded.
design_judgement.stated_ceiling: The builder's stated ceiling - that these checks read whether a phrase is present and where it sits, not what a prompt means - is accurate and was confirmed rather than defeated. It is also not the ceiling that bit here. The frame interior is not a limit of reading meaning; it is a branch that stops reading.

Is a landing admissible on a witness observation that cannot be schema-valid, given that no schema in contracts/ admits the six keys the gate requires? Every one of the ten observations in this directory has the same defect, and nothing grades the directory.
